title: A countably generated scalar-extension submodule lifts from the base
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $L$ be an $A$-module, and let $Q\subseteq B\otimes_A L$ be a countably generated $B$-submodule. Then there exists a countably generated $A$-submodule $P\subseteq L$ such that the image of the natural map $B\otimes_A P\to B\otimes_A L$ contains $Q$. Countably generated means that an at most countable subset spans by finite linear combinations.

proof.text: Write $f:A\to B$ for the ring map. Choose generators $(q_i)_{i\in I}$ of $Q$, where $I\subseteq\mathbb N$; an empty or finite $I$ is allowed. The tensor product is generated by pure tensors, by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so for each $i$ choose a finite expression $q_i=\sum_{j<n_i}b_{ij}\otimes x_{ij}$ with $b_{ij}\in B$ and $x_{ij}\in L$. Indeed an $A$-linear combination of pure tensors has this form by the balancing identity $a(b\otimes x)=(f(a)b)\otimes x$. Zero can be represented by the empty sum.

source.place: Tag 05A7, lemma-lift-countably-generated-submodule, proof: choose generators and write each as a finite tensor sum

proof.text: Let $T=\{(i,j)\in\mathbb N^2:i\in I,\ j<n_i\}$ and put $P=\operatorname{span}_A\{x_{ij}:(i,j)\in T\}\subseteq L$. Listing pairs of natural numbers in increasing order of $i+j$, and then increasing $i$, lists $\mathbb N^2$; retaining the pairs in $T$ shows that the family $(x_{ij})_{(i,j)\in T}$ has at most countably many members. Thus $P$ is countably generated by its displayed generators. This also gives $P=0$ if $T$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 05A7, lemma-lift-countably-generated-submodule, proof: take the submodule generated by the tensor factors

proof.text: Let $\iota:P\hookrightarrow L$. The tensor universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] applied to the $A$-bilinear map $(b,p)\mapsto b\otimes\iota(p)$ gives $v:B\otimes_A P\to B\otimes_A L$ with $v(b\otimes p)=b\otimes\iota(p)$. Both tensor products carry the $B$-action $c(b\otimes p)=(cb)\otimes p$ on the left factor. Hence $v(c(b\otimes p))=(cb)\otimes\iota(p)=c\,v(b\otimes p)$; additivity and generation by pure tensors extend this equality to every tensor, proving that $v$ is $B$-linear.

source.place: Tag 05A7, lemma-lift-countably-generated-submodule, statement: the natural tensor map; its construction by the tensor universal property

proof.text: For every $(i,j)\in T$, view $x_{ij}$ as $\widetilde x_{ij}\in P$ and set $z_i=\sum_{j<n_i}b_{ij}\otimes\widetilde x_{ij}\in B\otimes_A P$. The formula for $v$ from Step 3 and additivity give $v(z_i)=\sum_{j<n_i}b_{ij}\otimes x_{ij}=q_i$. Every $q\in Q$ is a finite $B$-linear combination $q=\sum_{i\in F}c_iq_i$ of the chosen generators, so $q=v(\sum_{i\in F}c_i z_i)$ by $B$-linearity. Consequently $Q\subseteq\operatorname{im}v$, as required.

source.place: Tag 05A7, lemma-lift-countably-generated-submodule, proof: the chosen factors lift the generators and hence their span
